newsitem.title: UK: British widow fights for right to husband's sperm.
newsitem.headline: British widow fights for right to husband's sperm.

text.p: A British woman is fighting a legal battle for permission to try to become pregnant through in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) with her dead husband's sperm, the Guardian newspaper reported on Monday.
The 30-year-old woman, who was not named, asked doctors to remove sperm from her husband before switching off his life support machine after he died last year from bacterial meningitis.

But Britain's Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority, which provoked a row earlier this year when it ordered the destruction of thousands of human foetuses created for IVF which had passed a legal deadline, says she cannot use the sperm because her dead husband had not give written permission.
The woman's case will be heard in the High Court in London on Wednesday and she could face costs of more than 80,000 pounds ($124,900) if she loses.
She and her husband, who married in 1991, had been trying to have a baby since the beginning of 1995 but he died before she could conceive, the Guardian said. ($1=.6405 Pound)
